reason: This passage (Exodus 32:25-29) describes the aftermath of the Golden Calf incident. While the Israelites do face severe punishment—three thousand men are killed—this is internal divine judgment and self-inflicted consequence for their own religious transgression (worshiping the Golden Calf), not oppression or persecution by an external people or power. The statement 'oppressed and persecuted as a people' typically refers to systematic subjugation by foreign nations or external enemies, whereas this text depicts internal communal punishment administered by the Levites on God's instruction as corrective action for the people's sin.
